**Example material · Synthetic observations · 18 October 2026**

## Fast enough for thought

An interface can respond instantly and still leave its reader waiting for understanding. The useful unit of speed is the complete decision, including the moments spent checking the evidence.

The example below imagines four versions of the same analytical page. These are invented timings, provided to demonstrate an interactive RichView report. They are not performance measurements of RichView or another product.

```chart
type: bar
title: "Interpretation time (seconds)"
data:
  inline:
    - {category: "A", value: 36}
    - {category: "B", value: 28}
    - {category: "C", value: 19}
    - {category: "D", value: 23}
encoding: {x: category, y: value}
axes:
  x: {label: Category}
  y: {label: "Interpretation time (seconds)"}
```

*Source: Fictional observations from an imaginary reading exercise; lower values are not a universal design objective.*

## What to take away

Version C gives the reader more context before presenting the chart. The imagined result suggests a question worth testing, not a causal conclusion. In a real study, keep task difficulty and reader familiarity visible alongside the timing.
